content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge resolves a chain-against-chain collision by noting that the text does not explicitly name whose body is the channel.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"the stating-verse test DG-61 retires — I weighed whether it bars only demanding an explicit contrary verse, or also bars using the absence of explicit naming as decisive for underdetermination.","why":"The judge's underdetermination turns on the text's not naming the channel, so it applies the retired explicit-statement test rather than weighing the competing chains by footing."}
